previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted from rehabilitation with acute onset substernal chest pain, worse with inspiration and lying flat. Initial concern was for acute coronary syndrome, but serial troponins were negative and EKG changes were nonspecific. The pain pattern and recent CABG suggested pericarditis, though echo showed no effusion. Elevated WBC and new infiltrate on CXR led to diagnosis of pneumonia, treated with IV vancomycin and cefepime. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic completion. Mild acute on chronic diastolic heart failure was managed with cautious diuresis. Her kidney function worsened slightly but stabilized. Metoprolol was held due to bradycardia and will be restarted at lower dose. She improved clinically, remained pain-free, and was discharged back to extended care with a plan for follow-up and sleep study for suspected OSA.

Brief Hospital Course:
Hospital course:

1. Upper GI Bleed: Patient with mild Hct decline (to nadir of 
___), with report of coffee ground emesis on admission. Likely 
secondary to ___ tear with maybe history of vomiting 
prior to coffee ground emesis.  Her hematocrit had remained 
stable throughout the hospitilization around her post-CABG 
baseline.  She did not require blood tranfusion.  She was on IV 
pantoprazole 40 mg BID which was switched to pantoprazole 40 mg 
po BID on the ___ floor which was eventually switched to 
omeprazole 40 mg po BID with concern for proton pump inhibitor 
induced Acute interstitial nephritis.  GI was consulted for 
endoscopy.  They suggested acute medical care of her pulmonary 
and renal status and no urgent need for endoscopy as patient has 
had stable Hematocrit.  Plavix was held throughout the hospital 
stay.
.
2. Shortness of breath: Likely secondary to pulmonary edema due 
to aggressive IV fluids in patient admitted with upper GI bleed 
and Acute Kidney injury.  Diuresed on lasix gtt with metalozone 
5 mg po BID and eventually switched to IV lasix 40 mg TID with 
metalozone 5 mg po BID.  Her shortness of breath improved with 
aggressive diuresis.  
.
3. Acute kidney injury, on chronic kidney disease: Patient with 
Cr 2.8 today with highest measured at 3.6 during the hospital 
stay with 2.7 on admission. Likely secondary to Acute 
interstitial nephritis vs hemodynamic cause.  Her creatinine did 
not respond to fluid resuscitation.  All medications were 
renally dosed and MAP was kept above 65.  Renal US did not show 
any renal artery pathology or intraparenchymal or obstructive 
pathology.  
.
4. UTI: Patient had an abnormal Urine analysis with fever on 
admission . She was treated empirically with 7 days of 
ciprofloxacin.  Her repeat Urine analysis and urine culture were 
negative.  
.
5. Constipation: Patient reports not having a bowel movement in 
one week.  She reports passsing gas and does not report 
abdominal pain.
.
6. Intractable nausea: Unsure of the etiology.  CT head without 
contrast was normal.  She was initially treated with IV Zofran 
for her nausea which resolved over the course of her hospital 
stay.

7. Non-functioning PICC line: PICC line was not functioning and 
Alteplase was attempted. IJ line placed for access in the 
setting of needing access for GI bleed and infection.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with history of recent CABG, on Plavix and
history of previous stroke, presents with intractable nausea, concern for
increased intracranial pressure.  Question of mass or hemorrhage.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to MRI obtained ___.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of acute hemorrhage, mass effect, large mass
or new infarct.  There are small hypodensities in the right ACA/MCA watershed
territory consistent with infarcts identified on MRI study ___ (2A:16
through 18).  The gray-white matter differentiation is preserved.  The sulci
and ventricles are slightly prominent, consistent with age-related parenchymal
volume loss.  On axial views, the cerebellar tonsils appear somewhat low
lying, however, sagittal reformations confirm position above the foramen
magnum.  There are no bony abnormalities identified.  Note is made of mild
soft tissue edema overlying the bilateral temporal bones and posterior
calvarium. ___ of the posterior arch of atlas is likely variant/old
trauma.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial hemorrhage or mass effect identified. To
correlate clinically and with ICP for raised intracranial pressure as CT is
less sensitive in the early stages and follow up as clinically indicated.

HISTORY:  Shortness of breath with prior CABG.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with the study of ___, there are lower lung volumes. 
There is continued enlargement of the cardiac silhouette with elevation of
pulmonary venous pressure in a patient with intact midline sternal sutures. 
Left central catheter remains in place.  The right PICC line appears to have
been removed.

INDICATION:  A ___ female with chronic kidney disease of unknown
etiology.

COMPARISON:  Renal ultrasound, ___.

FINDINGS:  Note was again made that this is a limited study due to the
patient's body habitus.  The right kidney measures 10.1 cm and the left kidney
measures 10.8 cm.  There is no hydronephrosis and no cyst or stone or solid
mass is seen in either kidney.

DOPPLER EXAMINATION:  Color Doppler and pulse-wave Doppler images were
obtained.  Appropriate venous waveforms are seen in the main renal vein of
each kidney.  Arterial waveforms with sharp upstrokes are seen in the main
renal artery of each kidney.  Resistive indices of the intraparenchymal
arteries are all 1.0 as no diastolic flow could be identified in any of the
waveforms bilaterally.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No hydronephrosis.
2.  No indication of renal artery stenosis.  Lack of diastolic flow in all of
the arterial waveforms bilaterally is suggestive of chronic parenchymal
disease.  Patent renal veins seen bilaterally.
